_ILLUSTRATIVE: EXAMPLE ONLY — every ID below is fabricated. This file documents the SHAPE that --node-map expects; it will not address any real component. Generate the real map with scripts/discover-node-map.js against the file you are working in, and keep it per project (context document, or a local cache outside this repo). Never commit a real map here: node IDs and property keys are specific to one file, and a skill carrying them applies one project's addressing to another.
_addressing: Suffixes are local node IDs, read from a LIVE INSTANCE's own children (never from a separately-resolved main-component node — see discover-node-map.js's header comment for why those two can disagree). For any instance, prefix each with 'I<instanceNodeId>;' to get the real node ID — instance 0:100 with suffix 0:200 gives 'I0:100;0:200'. This holds through plain (non-instance) frame nesting; Figma only adds another ';<suffix>' segment when crossing into a nested component instance.
_structure: The component's top level is [Title, Content]. 'Title' is a plain text layer holding the instance's own label (e.g. the colour or scale name). 'Content' is a plain frame wrapping [Spacer, 12 column headers, then 12 rows of (row header + 12 blocks)] — 169 children in total. 'Spacer' occupies the old top-left corner slot, needs no styling, and should not be touched.
_propertyKeys: The '#0:0' portion of a property key is generated per component and differs between files — read it from a real instance rather than assuming it. discover-node-map.js does this by matching the key prefix 'Label text#' and the property whose type is VARIANT. The header's variant is OPTIONAL and only used when isLightDarkPair is true — some libraries have no readability-toggle property at all and rely solely on the direct fill overrides build-matrix-script.py always applies.
